investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner never reached the agent-creation logic that would populate those fields.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm (resource quota exhausted or limit reached), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 131–146 seconds across all three checks, the eval runner timed out before createAgent() could return, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) empty and causing a full contract-validation failure. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion could be evaluated because evidence was empty.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: the 2 nodes that carry this resource had no remaining VM slots at the time all three eval pods were submitted, and preemption found no victims to evict.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's node affinity/selector rules exclude 4 of 6 nodes entirely, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes. If those selectors are overly restrictive or if node labels changed, capacity headroom is structurally limited.

Tertiary — cluster capacity under-provisioned for concurrent remote-agent workloads: three eval pods were submitted in close succession (11:03–11:11 UTC); if existing remote agent VMs were already consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, no capacity remained for the eval pods.

Lower confidence — transient spike in production remote agent usage at the time of the eval run consumed all VM slots before the eval pods could be scheduled; this would be a timing issue rather than a structural one.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A re-run of the eval that succeeds and returns vmIdPresent=true and a valid remoteState would indicate the scheduling failure was transient and capacity has since recovered.

Cluster node inspection showing kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity was available and unused on both eligible nodes at the time of the failure would suggest the pod spec itself (e.g., resource request quantity) is misconfigured rather than capacity being exhausted.
Evidence that the pod was scheduled but the agent process failed to start or reach a ready state would shift the root cause from scheduling to agent runtime initialization.
A passing run of remote-agent-create concurrent with a failing run of an unrelated check would confirm the issue is isolated to the scheduling layer and not a broader API or auth failure.
Scheduler logs showing the pod was eventually scheduled but the eval runner timed out before polling would indicate a latency/timeout configuration issue rather than a hard capacity ceiling.

Add a concurrent-capacity eval that submits a single remote agent pod and measures time-to-scheduled separately from time-to-ready, enabling distinction between scheduling latency and agent startup latency.
Consider adding a kata.peerpods.io/vm utilization threshold check as a warning-level eval that fires before capacity is fully exhausted, providing earlier signal than a full Unschedulable failure.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-07-06T11:06–11:11Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have no available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval pod could not be scheduled, the agent was never created, and the remote-agent-state check produced zero evidence — all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes that support the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient capacity (0 VMs available), and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure that prevented agent creation entirely, which in turn caused the remote-agent-state eval to produce no evidence and fail its expected-output contract. This is an eval-detected infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-06 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the eval pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state) is consistent across all three sibling checks, indicating the VM-capacity shortage is the shared upstream blocker. The eval pod was stuck unscheduled for 146 seconds before the check timed out, producing zero evidence output and causing the contract validation to fail on all five required fields. This is an eval infrastructure failure against the production Kubernetes cluster; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all three sibling checks report the identical 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message, indicating the VM-slot resource advertised by the Kata PeerPods device plugin is at zero on both eligible nodes at the time of each eval run.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or label drift: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's affinity/selector, leaving only 2 nodes eligible. If those labels changed or the selector became overly restrictive, the effective scheduling pool shrank to the 2 already-saturated nodes.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie eval pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: prior eval runs that did not clean up their remote-agent pods could hold VM slots, preventing new pods from scheduling. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1916) is intended to prevent this, but a prior crash or timeout could bypass cleanup.

Quaternary — Kata PeerPods device plugin reporting incorrect or stale capacity: the plugin may have failed to reclaim VM slots after previous pod terminations, causing the node to advertise zero available VMs even if the underlying peer-pod VMs have been released.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner never reached the agent-creation logic that would populate those fields.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm (resource quota exhausted or limit reached), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 131–146 seconds across all three checks, the eval runner timed out before createAgent() could return, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) empty and causing a full contract-validation failure. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: the 2 nodes that carry this resource had no remaining VM slots at the time all three eval pods were submitted, and preemption found no victims to evict.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's node affinity/selector rules exclude 4 of 6 nodes entirely, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes. If those selectors are overly restrictive or if node labels changed, capacity headroom is structurally limited.

Tertiary — cluster capacity under-provisioned for concurrent remote-agent workloads: three eval pods were submitted in close succession (11:03–11:11 UTC); if existing remote agent VMs were already consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, no capacity remained for the eval pods.

Lower confidence — transient spike in production remote agent usage at the time of the eval run consumed all VM slots before the eval pods could be scheduled; this would be a timing issue rather than a structural one.

Quaternary — Kata PeerPods device plugin reporting incorrect or stale capacity: the plugin may have failed to reclaim VM slots after previous pod terminations, causing the node to advertise zero available VMs even if the underlying peer-pod VMs have been released.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of remote-agent-runtime that produces all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) would disprove that VM capacity is currently exhausted.

Node capacity inspection showing kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable > 0 on the affinity-eligible nodes at the time of the failure would suggest the scheduler message was transient or caused by a different resource contention.
Evidence that the pod's node affinity/selector was misconfigured (e.g., selecting zero nodes) rather than VM exhaustion would shift the primary cause to a selector misconfiguration.
A passing run of remote-agent-create or remote-agent-state while remote-agent-runtime fails would suggest the failure is isolated to the runtime check rather than a shared scheduling pool problem.
Confirmation that no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exists on any node (plugin not installed) would indicate a cluster configuration regression rather than capacity exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on all affinity-eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct check status rather than a scheduling timeout.
Add a leaked-pod detection eval that lists all pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots in the eval namespace and fails if any are in a non-Running state beyond a configurable age threshold.
Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies at least N nodes match the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector and that those nodes collectively advertise sufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity.

Consider adding a historical baseline to the remote-agent-runtime check (verifierContext.history shows previousRunCount=0 and lastPassingAt=null); establishing a passing baseline would enable regression detection on future runs.
